key_insight: A physics-grounded digital twin can rapidly screen robotic welding settings and controller actions for in-space metal joining before expensive flight-like tests.
engineering_relevance: This work helps de-risk on-orbit manufacturing by combining reduced-order thermal physics, surrogate models, and robot control to predict weld quality under constrained space-environment conditions.
method: Finite-volume weld-pool thermal model with solid-liquid phase change, effective thermocapillary transport, and local-pressure effects.
Gaussian-process and neural-network surrogates trained and validated with repeated five-fold cross-validation.
Simulated six-axis manipulator study with closed-loop proportional control for a UR5 L-shaped seam.
evidence_signal: Across 10 held-out boundary cases, 74 of 80 solver responses fell within nominal 90% GP predictive intervals, and the GP outperformed the neural network on all eight outputs in repeated cross-validation.
watch_item: The controller and model are still simulation-based, so thermal-vacuum, reduced-gravity, and hardware-in-the-loop testing are needed before operational deployment.
paper_title: De-Risking Robotic Welding for In-Space Metal Joining Through Physics-Grounded Digital Twins
